events.title: The Black Hole of Calcutta
events.description: After Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah's forces captured Fort William in Calcutta, British prisoners were confined overnight in a tiny cell. Many of them died from heat and suffocation.
events.significance: The episode became a rallying point for British colonial propaganda. It fed into the Battle of Plassey the following year, which opened the way for East India Company rule in Bengal.

events.title: Congress Adopts the Great Seal of the United States
events.description: The Continental Congress approved the design of the Great Seal. It shows an eagle clutching an olive branch and arrows, and the motto E Pluribus Unum.
events.significance: The seal is still used to authenticate official documents. Its imagery remains a lasting emblem of American sovereignty.

events.title: The Tennis Court Oath
events.description: Locked out of their usual meeting hall at Versailles, deputies of France's Third Estate gathered in a nearby indoor tennis court. They swore not to disband until France had a written constitution.
events.significance: The oath was a decisive act of defiance against royal authority. It marked a turning point in the early French Revolution.

events.title: The Siege of the Legations Begins in Beijing
events.description: During the Boxer Rebellion, Imperial Chinese forces began a siege of the Legation Quarter, where foreign diplomats and civilians had taken shelter. It lasted 55 days.
events.significance: An international force ended the siege, and the aftermath deepened foreign influence over a weakening Qing dynasty.

events.title: Death of Neda Agha-Soltan
events.description: During protests following Iran's disputed presidential election, Neda Agha-Soltan was fatally shot in Tehran. Her death was captured on video and spread rapidly online.
events.significance: The footage made her a global symbol of the protest movement. It showed how social media could carry a political crisis to a worldwide audience.
